title: Knowledge check: Reliability and Graceful Shutdown

questions.prompt: In Reliability and Graceful Shutdown, which statement best describes Stopping acceptance of new work?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.

Connect this syllabus point to Reliability and Graceful Shutdown: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
This option describes a different concept and does not define stopping acceptance of new work (choice 2).

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Reliability and Graceful Shutdown?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.

questions.prompt: A change related to Reliability and Graceful Shutdown appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
